children: on Wednesday lost more than 7% in premarket trading after becoming the latest U.S. healthcare company to report a data breach following a 'material' cybersecurity incident at its subsidiary Astrana Health Management.

In a regulatory filing, the Alhambra, California-based healthcare services platform disclosed that threat actors impersonating company personnel have gained access to "certain private and/or confidential information" maintained on its servers.
They conducted the hack using multiple social engineering attempts, contacting certain employees through the company’s main telephone number, Astrana
said, adding that an investigation is underway into the incident, which it described as “material” as of Sept. 22.
While the company has yet to estimate the full scope of the incident, it says there won’t be a material impact on its financial condition and results of operations.
Multiple U.S.-based healthcare companies, including Boston Scientific
, have all reported cybersecurity events this year, and Astrana’s
came close on the heels of a short report from GlassHouse
